title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten named Twin Cities destinations where UMN students can spend time with art, exhibits, nature, or friends without admission or a purchase.

cards.title: Browse the Weisman galleries
cards.subtitle: East Bank, University of Minnesota Twin Cities
cards.notes: Meet at the museum entrance, move through the galleries at your own pace, and use the building’s riverfront setting as a natural conversation break.
cards.short_summary: A campus art-museum visit with free admission for everyone.
cards.evidence_claim: Weisman Art Museum states that it offers free admission to all.
cards.source_title: Make a Gift | Weisman Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open to students and the general public; check the museum’s current visitor information before going.

cards.title: Walk the Bell Museum galleries
cards.subtitle: 2088 Larpenteur Ave W, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Bring a valid student ID, reserve or ask at arrival as directed, then explore the natural-history galleries together without adding a planetarium ticket.
cards.short_summary: UMN students can enter the museum galleries free with student ID.
cards.evidence_claim: Bell Museum lists Museum Gallery Admission for UMN students with student ID as free; planetarium shows cost extra.
cards.access_notes: Valid UMN student ID is required for free gallery admission. Planetarium admission is not included.

cards.title: Take a garden walk at the Arboretum
cards.subtitle: University of Minnesota Landscape Arboretum, Chaska
cards.notes: Call ahead to book the required student ticket, bring your U Card and UMN email access, then choose a garden or trail for an unhurried group walk.
cards.short_summary: A student-ID-supported garden and trail outing at the university’s Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum states that current University of Minnesota students receive complimentary admission and must call to book tickets.
cards.source_title: Ticket Details | University of Minnesota Landscape Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Current UMN students must call 612-301-6775 to book complimentary admission; bring required student credentials.

cards.title: Make a self-guided sculpture loop
cards.subtitle: 726 Vineland Place, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Pick a few works to discuss, pause at Spoonbridge and Cherry, and use the free digital guide if your group wants artwork context while walking.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor public-art walk with no ticket or admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walker states that the Minneapolis Sculpture Garden requires no tickets and is always free to the public.
cards.source_title: Minneapolis Sculpture Garden | Walker Art Center
cards.access_notes: Open daily, 6 a.m.–midnight year-round according to the Walker; parking may have a charge.

cards.title: See an Andersen Library exhibition
cards.subtitle: West Bank; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Check what is currently installed, then use the gallery and atrium displays as a low-key stop before or after time on the West Bank.
cards.short_summary: Free library exhibitions in the university’s archives and special-collections building.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, and identifies Andersen Library exhibition spaces.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Others need an appointment.

cards.title: Look through a Rapson Hall exhibit
cards.subtitle: Rapson Hall; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Coordinate a quick meet-up in Rapson Hall, look over the library’s exhibit area, and leave time to compare details that caught each person’s eye.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost campus exhibit stop inside Rapson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Architecture and Landscape Architecture Library in Rapson Hall.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

cards.title: Visit a Vincent Hall library exhibit
cards.subtitle: Vincent Hall; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Use the exhibit cases as a brief study-break destination, then continue the hang with a walk across Northrop Mall or nearby campus paths.
cards.short_summary: Free exhibition viewing in the Mathematics Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Mathematics Library in Vincent Hall.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

cards.title: Check out a Ferguson Hall exhibit
cards.subtitle: Ferguson Hall; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Stop in between classes or rehearsals, spend a few minutes with the display cases, and use the visit as an easy starting point for a campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A free exhibit-focused visit to the Music Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Music Library in Ferguson Hall.

cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

cards.subtitle: Hodson Hall; library exhibitions

cards.subtitle: Phillips-Wangensteen Building; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Plan a focused visit to the historical-library display area, read labels together, and keep the hang simple by discussing one item each person noticed.
